questions.question: What mask ratio does cosine_schedule(T=8) return at its first step?
options: 0.000, because sampling begins with every token visible
0.500, because the midpoint is used for the first prediction
About 0.981, from cos(pi/16), so almost all positions remain masked initially
1.500, because cosine values are shifted above one
questions.explanation: The schedule uses cos(pi*(t+1)/(2*T)). At t=0 and T=8 this is cos(pi/16) ≈ 0.981, a high initial mask ratio.

questions.question: What does step_unmask do with a token list containing MASK entries?
options: It changes every position, including already visible tokens
It masks the lowest-confidence visible tokens and never predicts replacements
It copies the prompt seed into every masked position
It predicts masked positions, ranks their confidences, and fills only the requested top fraction
questions.explanation: The helper obtains mock logits for masked entries, sorts masked indices by predicted probability, and replaces only n_to_keep positions. Existing tokens are retained.

questions.question: How is the initial state in sample(prompt_seed=3, T=8) represented?
options: A list of 16 MASK=-1 entries
Sixteen random vocabulary IDs sampled before the first step
A single MASK token shared by all positions
A list containing the prompt seed at each position
questions.explanation: sample initializes tokens = [MASK] * SEQ_LEN, and SEQ_LEN is 16. The trace therefore begins with sixteen unknown image-token positions.

questions.question: Which task is not one of the four uses listed for the Show-o checkpoint?
options: Text generation with standard NTP
Audio transcription from a waveform
Text-to-image generation with masked image tokens
Image inpainting through the same masked loop
questions.explanation: The driver lists text generation, VQA, T2I, and inpainting. Audio transcription is not part of this checkpoint's four-task demonstration.

questions.question: Why does sample keep calling step_unmask after the scheduled steps if MASK entries remain?
options: To re-mask every token and restart the cosine schedule
To change the vocabulary size after diffusion finishes
To force a final fill pass so the returned sequence contains no MASK values
To evaluate an audio decoder on the residual mask
questions.explanation: The while any(t == MASK for t in tokens) loop uses keep_ratio=1.0 until every position has a sampled ID. It guarantees a complete discrete sequence.

questions.question: What qualitative behavior does the cosine schedule encourage in this sampler?
options: A fixed number of tokens is unmasked at every step
Only the final step can change an image token
The sampler keeps a high mask ratio forever, preventing completion
It moves from many masked positions toward fewer masked positions with a smooth coarse-to-fine reveal
questions.explanation: The cosine values fall from near one toward zero. Since keep_ratio is based on 1-ratio, progressively more positions are revealed as sampling advances.
